title: Sadhana Mittal — demand notice relegated to Supply Code objection remedy
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Ashok Bhushan, J.; Abhinava Upadhya, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to Supply Code statutory remedy.
headnote: A writ to quash a demand notice issued in another person's name was disposed of without examining merits. The Division Bench held that the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a statutory remedy of raising objections against an electricity bill or charges, which the petitioner may avail.
facts: Smt. Sadhana Mittal filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court seeking quashing of a demand notice dated 5 May 2012 issued in the name of one Shanti Devi. She submitted that she had already filed an objection, addressed to the Managing Director and annexed as Annexure-3, which had not been considered. Counsel for the petitioner and Sri A.L. Yadav for the respondents were heard. The Court did not examine the demand, the billed identity, or the pending objection on merits.

holding_units.topic: statutory remedy — objections to electricity bill or charges
holding_units.holding: Under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 the consumer has a statutory remedy of raising objections against an electricity bill or electricity charges; where that remedy is available, the writ court will not examine the demand and will leave the petitioner to avail it. The petition was disposed of with that observation.
holding_units.flag: Court cited the Supply Code 2005 generally for objections to bill/charges; clause 6.8 is inferred, not numbered in the order.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand notice dated 5.5.2012 is liable to be quashed, and whether a demand in the name of Shanti Devi binds the petitioner
not_decided.note: Pending objection to the Managing Director also not examined.
